chapter.v:
Why do
the nations rage,And the peoples meditate a vain thing?

The kings
of the earth set themselves,And the rulers take counsel together,Against Jehovah, and against his anointed, saying,

Let us
break their bonds asunder,And cast away their cords from us.

He that
sitteth in the heavens will laugh:The Lord will have them in derision.

Then will
he speak unto them in his wrath,And vex them in his sore displeasure:

Yet I
have set my kingUpon my holy hill of Zion.

I will
tell of the decree:Jehovah said unto me, Thou art my son;This day have I begotten thee.

Ask of
me, and I will give thee the nations for thine inheritance,And the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.

Thou shalt
break them with a rod of iron;Thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

Now therefore
be wise, O ye kings:Be instructed, ye judges of the earth.

Serve Jehovah
with fear,And rejoice with trembling.

Kiss the
son, lest he be angry, and ye perish in the way,For his wrath will soon be kindled.Blessed are all they that take refuge in him.
